overview: At Abomey, the royal palaces combined government, skilled craft production and the storage of royal treasures. Their architecture and imagery expressed Aja-Fon traditions and preserved memories of successive rulers.

items.text: Palace builders used earthen walls and traditional materials to organize enclosed compounds around courtyards.
Polychrome reliefs gave palace walls a visual language of royal history and symbolism.
Outer, inner and private courtyards structured access through each palace, making social distinctions part of the built environment.
Royal families continue ceremonies and care for sacred places, including royal tombs and structures associated with a king's spirit.
